sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》，我是瑞切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: When Spirit Airlines shut down over the weekend, it brought an end to a company that had revolutionized air travel in the United States with an ultra-low-cost approach.
sentences.zh: 当精神航空在周末倒闭时，它标志着一家以超低成本模式彻底革新美国航空旅行的公司的终结。

sentences.en: So today, I talked to my colleague, Neeraj Chakshi, about the so-called spirit effect on air travel, why it unraveled,
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我采访了我的同事尼拉杰·查克希，聊了聊所谓的“精神效应”对航空旅行的影响、它为何走向瓦解，

sentences.en: and whether the problems that doomed spirit could spread to other airlines.
sentences.zh: 以及导致精神航空毁灭的问题是否会蔓延到其他航空公司。

sentences.en: And my colleague, Lindsay Garrison, talks to a spirit flight attendant about what spirit represented.
sentences.zh: 我的同事林赛·加里森采访了一名精神航空的空乘，聊了聊精神航空代表着什么。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, May 7.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月7日，星期四。

sentences.en: Lindsay, this is Colleen.
sentences.zh: 林赛，这是科琳。

sentences.en: Oh, hey, Colleen.
sentences.zh: 哦，嘿，科琳。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Hey, nice to meet you as well.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我也很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Thank you again for your time.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: I'm really grateful.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: And just to say, I'm really sorry that this is the circumstance under which we're talking, but I really thank you again.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，对于我们交谈的这种背景，我感到非常遗憾，但我还是要再次感谢你。

sentences.en: Could we just start by you just telling me a little bit about, you know, who you are and when you started working for Spirit Airlines?
sentences.zh: 我们能从你简单介绍一下自己，以及你是什么时候开始为精神航空工作的开始吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, um, my name is Colleen Burns and I am a Spirit Airlines flight attendant.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我叫科琳·伯恩斯，我是精神航空的一名空乘。

sentences.en: And I was, um, it sounds crazy to say, I was Spirit Airlines flight attendant for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我，嗯，说出来听着挺疯狂的，我做精神航空的空乘有10年了。

sentences.en: I'd actually just started my 11th year with the company.
sentences.zh: 其实我刚开始在这家公司的第11个年头。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Do you remember your first day on the job?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你上班的第一天吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was so nervous.
sentences.zh: 记得，我当时太紧张了。

sentences.en: And I just remember that first crew, like when I got there, they were like, so incredibly kind to me.
sentences.zh: 我只记得第一批机组人员，当我到那儿的时候，他们对我都好得难以置信。

sentences.en: They were like, oh my God, it's your first flight.
sentences.zh: 他们说，天哪，这是你的第一次飞行。

sentences.en: Like, sometimes we, it happened more back in the day, um, but we used to pull pranks on each other when you were a new flight attendant.
sentences.zh: 就好像，有时候我们，过去这种事更多一些，嗯，但以前当你是个新空乘时，我们会互相恶作剧。

sentences.en: And so they had the pilots tell me that something was wrong with the air in the cabin and that I had to do an air test and I needed to collect an air
sentences.zh: 所以他们让飞行员告诉我，客舱里的空气出了问题，我必须做一次空气测试，我需要收集一个空气

sentences.en: sample in a trash bag and bring it into the cockpit.
sentences.zh: 样本放到垃圾袋里，然后带进驾驶舱。

sentences.en: And I was like, I don't remember learning about this at all.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，我根本不记得学过这个啊。

sentences.en: And like, oh my gosh, I didn't retain anything.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我什么都没记住。

sentences.en: So I'm like walking through this cabin on my very first flight operating as a flight attendant with a giant white trash bag above my head, collecting air.
sentences.zh: 所以我拿着一个巨大的白色垃圾袋套在头上，在客舱里走来走去，作为一名空乘执行我的第一次飞行，收集空气。

sentences.en: I go into the cockpit and the pilots both look at me and just start busting out laughing, busting out laughing.
sentences.zh: 我走进驾驶舱，两位飞行员看着我，然后开始哈哈大笑，放声大笑。

sentences.en: But we used to do silly things like that to one another all the time.
sentences.zh: 但我们以前经常对彼此做这种傻事。

sentences.en: And it's something that I just don't, I don't hear those stories from other airlines.
sentences.zh: 而且这是我在其他航空公司听不到的故事。

sentences.en: And there's just something really special about being a Spirit flight attendant.
sentences.zh: 当精神航空的空乘有一种非常特别的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: What, what is it, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是什么，到底是什么？

sentences.en: Like, what is that thing?
sentences.zh: 那种感觉是什么？

sentences.en: I, I think that Spirit has been through so many like changes and like revivals and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我，我认为精神航空经历了那么多的改变和复苏，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: we went from being like the absolute most hated airline to, to be honest, towards the end, like people loved us.
sentences.zh: 我们从绝对最受讨厌的航空公司，说实话，到最后，人们开始爱我们。

sentences.en: And I think all of us went through that journey with Spirit and we all had so much pride in how far Spirit had come.
sentences.zh: 我想我们所有人都和精神航空一起经历了这段旅程，我们都为精神航空取得的成就感到无比自豪。

sentences.en: I mean, we're the underdog story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们是个逆袭的故事。

sentences.en: And I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我当时根本不知道。

sentences.en: None of, you know, we, we really all thought that Spirit was going to pull through.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都，你知道的，我们真的都以为精神航空能挺过去。

sentences.en: So, Neeraj, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Hey, thank you.
sentences.zh: 嘿，谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So, Neeraj, as you know, Spirit Airlines, they went under over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，如你所知，精神航空在周末破产了。

sentences.en: And this comes after the White House had tried to save the airline.
sentences.zh: 而此前白宫曾试图拯救这家航空公司。

sentences.en: They did not save the airline.
sentences.zh: 他们没有救下这家航空公司。

sentences.en: And what was so interesting was that this airline that had basically been a punchline for years sparked so much grief.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，这家多年来基本上沦为笑柄的航空公司引发了如此多的悲伤。

sentences.en: There was this outpouring of people talking about how sad they were that it was going away.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷表达他们对这家公司消亡的难过之情。

sentences.en: Our colleague, Lindsay Garrison, talked to a flight attendant who said how much the airline meant to her and how much she saw that the airline meant to other people.
sentences.zh: 我们的同事林赛·加里森采访了一位空乘，她诉说了这家航空公司对她的重大意义，以及她看到这家航空公司对其他人的重要性。

sentences.en: And so I want to start this conversation with you explaining to us why the death of this airline has struck such a chord with people.
sentences.zh: 所以我想通过请你向我们解释为什么这家航空公司的消亡会引起人们的强烈共鸣，来开始我们今天的对话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Spirit Airlines was this symbol of affordable travel in America.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，精神航空一直是美国经济实惠旅行的象征。

sentences.en: It allowed people to take trips that they couldn't otherwise afford.
sentences.zh: 它让人们能够进行原本负担不起的旅行。

sentences.en: For a large segment of the population, it was the only way for them to be able to fly to places.
sentences.zh: 对于很大一部分人口来说，这是他们能够飞往各地唯一的出行方式。

sentences.en: And the end came really suddenly.
sentences.zh: 而它的结束非常突然。

sentences.en: They decided late last week it was time to wind down.
sentences.zh: 他们上周晚些时候决定开始善后清盘。

sentences.en: And by Saturday morning, they shut down.
sentences.zh: 到周六早晨，他们就关门停业了。

sentences.en: That left 17,000 people who were directly employed or indirectly employed by Spirit out of work.
sentences.zh: 这导致17000名直接或间接受雇于精神航空的人失业。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of people who had tickets no longer had flights.
sentences.zh: 成千上万持有机票的人再也无法乘机了。

sentences.en: And it left a gaping hole in the airline market.
sentences.zh: 它在航空市场留下了一个巨大的空白。

sentences.en: I wonder if you could rewind the clock a little bit and tell us about where this airline came from.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能把时间倒回一点，给我们讲讲这家航空公司是怎么来的。

sentences.en: What was its origin story?
sentences.zh: 它的起源故事是什么？

sentences.en: And how did it end up symbolizing low-cost air travel in the United
sentences.zh: 它是如何最终成为美国低成本航空旅行的

sentences.en: States?
sentences.zh: 象征的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Spirit's origin actually dates all the way back to the 60s.
sentences.zh: 所以精神航空的起源实际上可以追溯到上世纪60年代。

sentences.en: It started as a trucking company.
sentences.zh: 它最初是一家货运公司。

sentences.en: They got into travel.
sentences.zh: 后来涉足旅游业。

sentences.en: They got into charter flights.
sentences.zh: 后来又涉足包机业务。

sentences.en: They renamed to Spirit Airlines in 92.
sentences.zh: 1992年更名为精神航空。

sentences.en: But most people didn't really know who they were.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人其实并不知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the mid-2000s that Spirit adopted the business model that we all know it for.
sentences.zh: 直到2000年代中期，精神航空才采用我们如今熟知的商业模式。

sentences.en: And that's the ultra-low-cost air travel model.
sentences.zh: 也就是超低成本航空旅行模式。

sentences.en: The idea is simple.
sentences.zh: 这个理念很简单。

sentences.en: You just cut costs as much as you can and you pass that along to passengers in the form of cheap fares.
sentences.zh: 就是尽可能地削减成本，然后以便宜票价的形式让利给乘客。

sentences.en: It was popularized in Europe by Ryanair, which is still going strong today.
sentences.zh: 这种模式由瑞安航空在欧洲推广开来，至今仍蒸蒸日上。

sentences.en: And they thought that they could bring it to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己也可以把这种模式带到美国

sentences.en: with success.
sentences.zh: 并取得成功。

sentences.en: And can you just explain that model?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这种模式吗？

sentences.en: Like, what did they do or cut to actually keep those ticket prices so low?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们做了什么或者削减了什么来保持如此低廉的票价？

sentences.en: Yeah, they did a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们做了很多。

sentences.en: The key thing that they did, which we all know them for, is unbundling.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的核心事情，也是我们所熟知的，就是拆分服务。

sentences.en: Why should we have to raise everybody's ticket price when only some people want to eat or drink on board?
sentences.zh: 为什么只有少数人在机上想吃东西或喝饮料时，我们就得提高所有人的票价？

sentences.en: We don't think that's fair.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这不公平。

sentences.en: We think it gives customers more choice.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这为客户提供了更多的选择。

sentences.en: And the real champion of this idea was Spirit's chief executive at the time, Ben Beldonza.
sentences.zh: 这个理念真正的倡导者是精神航空当时的首席执行官本·贝尔多萨。

sentences.en: Customers are welcome to bring water on the plane with them.
sentences.zh: 客户完全可以带水上飞机。

sentences.en: We're not stopping that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会阻止这一点。

sentences.en: But we sell what we sell.
sentences.zh: 但我们卖我们卖的东西。

sentences.en: They started to separate everything out so that seat assignments cost extra money, even water you're paying for carry-ons, having them print your boarding pass.
sentences.zh: 他们开始把所有东西都拆分开来，选座位要额外收费，连喝水、带随身行李、打印登机牌都要付钱。

sentences.en: But the seat itself could be really cheap.
sentences.zh: 但座位本身可以非常便宜。

sentences.en: So if you didn't need some of those things, you could actually buy a really dear cheap ticket.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不需要其中某些东西，你实际上可以买到一张非常非常便宜的机票。

sentences.en: I didn't realize this, that they literally charge you to print your boarding pass.
sentences.zh: 我以前没意识到这一点，他们连打印登机牌都要收钱。

sentences.en: It's like they're charging for everything except flying.
sentences.zh: 这就好像除了飞行本身，他们对什么都收费。

sentences.en: Like, everything else is considered a luxury just to keep the ticket as cheap as possible.
sentences.zh: 比如，为了让机票尽可能便宜，其他一切都被视为一种奢侈品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the idea is that, you know, some people don't need it.
sentences.zh: 而且这个理念是，你知道的，有些人不需要这些。

sentences.en: They're happy to pull it up on their phones or they don't need customer service.
sentences.zh: 他们很高兴在手机上调出登机牌，或者他们不需要客户服务。

sentences.en: So why would they pay the extra fee for it?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么要为此支付额外的费用呢？

sentences.en: I recognize our airline's not for everyone.
sentences.zh: 我承认我们的航空公司并不适合所有人。

sentences.en: If you want to be coddled in the airport, if you want an enormous amount of legroom, if you want a free Coke, we're not your airline.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在机场受到娇惯，如果你想要巨大的腿部空间，如果你想要一罐免费的可乐，我们不是你的航空公司。

sentences.en: And we're not built to be that airline.
sentences.zh: 我们生来就不是那样的航空公司。

sentences.en: But if you want to save $150 round trip, we're a great deal come fly us.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想在往返行程中省下150美元，我们是个划算的选择，来坐我们的飞机吧。

sentences.en: And they publicized this all with these racy, provocative ads.
sentences.zh: 他们通过这些性感、挑逗的广告来宣传这一切。

sentences.en: One of them was what they call the MILF sale.
sentences.zh: 其中一个广告就是他们所谓的MILF促销。

sentences.en: That's an acronym that some people may know.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有些人可能知道的缩写。

sentences.en: It's kind of a raunchy meaning.
sentences.zh: 它带有一种有些低俗的含义。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: From American Pie, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我记得出自《美国派》电影。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: But for Spirit, you know, it means many islands, low fares.
sentences.zh: 但对精神航空来说，你知道的，这代表着“许多岛屿，低廉票价”（Many Islands, Low Fares）。

sentences.en: A gross expression taken from the movie American Pie was adopted by Spirit Airlines.
sentences.zh: 这个借用自电影《美国派》的粗俗词汇被精神航空采纳了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, and they go viral, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，它们病毒式传播了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they're not only getting a lot of attention on their own, but, you know, news organizations start to cover them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们不仅自己获得了大量关注，而且，新闻机构也开始报道它们。

sentences.en: Spirit Airlines has a $69 campaign that, you know, if you don't understand the 69 reference, then Google it.
sentences.zh: 精神航空有一个69美元的活动，你知道的，如果你不明白69这个梗，那就去谷歌一下。

sentences.en: They start selling tickets for numbers that, you know, have other meanings for, you know, let's say $69.
sentences.zh: 他们开始以一些在你知道的方面有特殊含义的数字来卖机票，比方说69美元。

sentences.en: I didn't know any of this.
sentences.zh: 我之前对这些一无所知。

sentences.en: I am horrified.
sentences.zh: 我感到震惊。

sentences.en: Social media is buzzing about this.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体上对此议论纷纷。

sentences.en: On our Fox 29 Facebook page, Laurie wrote, how about grow up?
sentences.zh: 在我们福克斯29台的脸书主页上，劳瑞写道，成熟一点行吗？

sentences.en: Victoria wrote, I read the ad and kept waiting to be shocked.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚写道，我读了广告，一直在等待被震惊到。

sentences.en: So much hoopla over that.
sentences.zh: 为这事大惊小怪的。

sentences.en: And Spirit starts to get a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 精神航空开始获得大量关注。

sentences.en: People start to kind of get to know this airline.
sentences.zh: 人们开始慢慢了解这家航空公司。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: More ads means more controversy, means more news coverage, which means more attention.
sentences.zh: 更多的广告意味着更多的争议，意味着更多的新闻报道，这也意味着更多的关注。

sentences.en: But beyond all of that, how is the actual business model received?
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，实际的商业模式反响如何？

sentences.en: Like, given the fact that the business model itself was kind of a novel idea here in the United States?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这种商业模式本身在美国算是一个新颖的创意？

sentences.en: Yeah, there was a lot of skepticism.
sentences.zh: 是的，当时存在很多怀疑。

sentences.en: Consumers saw it as nickel and diming them.
sentences.zh: 消费者认为这是在变相敲竹杠、斤斤计较。

sentences.en: Investors had doubts that people would really want to fly on an airline like this or that the model could work.
sentences.zh: 投资者则怀疑人们是否真的想坐这样的航空公司，或者这种模式是否行得通。

sentences.en: And they were the butt of a lot of jokes.
sentences.zh: 他们成了许多笑话的嘲笑对象。

sentences.en: This is pretty crazy here.
sentences.zh: 这在这里确实挺疯狂的。

sentences.en: Spirit Airlines is considering a new fee to talk with a human face-to-face during check-in.
sentences.zh: 精神航空正在考虑收取一项新费用，用于在值机时与真人面对面交谈。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which explains the company's new slogan,
sentences.zh: 这就解释了该公司的新标语：

sentences.en: Spirit Airlines.
sentences.zh: 精神航空。

sentences.en: Why are you flying Spirit Airlines?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要坐精神航空？

sentences.en: I mean, on late night shows, the idea that like you would have to pay for a water bottle while flying or a printed boarding pass.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在深夜秀节目中，人们总觉得坐飞机时还要为一瓶水或打印登机牌付钱。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just outrageous.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这简直太离谱了。

sentences.en: The CEO of Spirit Airlines said, people shouldn't come to Spirit if they want lots of legroom.
sentences.zh: 精神航空的首席执行官曾说，如果乘客想要很多腿部空间，就别来精神航空。

sentences.en: He said, we call it Spirit Airlines because there's only enough room for your spirit.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们叫精神航空（Spirit Airlines），是因为这里只够容纳你的精神（spirit）。

sentences.en: And if I'm being honest, even that's going to get a little crushed.
sentences.zh: 说实话，连精神恐怕都要被挤压得有点变形了。

sentences.en: But, you know, they embraced it.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，他们接受了这种定位。

sentences.en: And when they got criticism, they would push back and say, look, we're here to make travel affordable.
sentences.zh: 每当受到批评时，他们就会反驳说，听着，我们来这里就是为了让旅行变得经济实惠。

sentences.en: That's what this is about.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键所在。

sentences.en: And take it or leave it.
sentences.zh: 爱搭不搭，随你便。

sentences.en: And it was slow at first, but then people start to fly in Spirit and it starts to pick up.
sentences.zh: 起步时进展缓慢，但后来人们开始选择精神航空，业务也开始有所起色。

sentences.en: And they go public in 2011.
sentences.zh: 他们于2011年上市。

sentences.en: And by the next year, they're flying about 10 million passengers.
sentences.zh: 到了第二年，他们的载客量就达到了约1000万人次。

sentences.en: They're doing really well.
sentences.zh: 他们发展得非常顺利。

sentences.en: And by 2016, they're up to 20 million passengers.
sentences.zh: 到2016年，载客量已经飙升至2000万人次。

sentences.en: And what was behind all that growth?
sentences.zh: 所有这些增长背后的原因是什么？

sentences.en: I can't imagine it was just the racy MILF ads.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象仅仅靠那些火辣成熟女性的广告就能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, they are stealing travelers from other airlines.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实在从其他航空公司那里抢夺旅客。

sentences.en: But there's also this idea that they're bringing people in off the sidelines.
sentences.zh: 但还有这样一种观点，即他们正在把原本不怎么出门的人吸引进来。

sentences.en: So people who normally wouldn't be flying, but they see an opportunity because the flights are cheap enough.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，那些平时可能不会坐飞机的人，因为机票足够便宜而看到了出行的机会。

sentences.en: They might be making that choice instead of ordering takeout.
sentences.zh: 他们做这个决定时，可能觉得这比点外卖还划算。

sentences.en: And this is something that Ben Baldonzo himself says, is he's like, we're not necessarily competing just with other airlines.
sentences.zh: 正如本·巴尔多佐（Ben Baldonzo）自己所说的那样，我们不一定只是在与其他航空公司竞争。

sentences.en: We're competing with other forms of spending.
sentences.zh: 我们在与消费者其他的消费形式竞争。

sentences.en: And this new approach that Spirit has is starting to affect the wider industry, where when Spirit enters an airport for the first time, you see fares drop.
sentences.zh: 精神航空这种新颖的运营方式开始对整个行业产生影响，每当精神航空首次进入某个机场时，你就会发现机票价格随之下降。

sentences.en: Other airlines have to compete.
sentences.zh: 其他航空公司不得不参与竞争。

sentences.en: And so they have to reduce their fares.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们也不得不降低票价。

sentences.en: It actually becomes the subject of academic study.
sentences.zh: 这甚至成为了学术研究的主题。

sentences.en: It's called the Spirit effect.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“精神效应”。

sentences.en: Did you feel like Spirit was different than other airlines?
sentences.zh: 你觉得精神航空跟其他航空公司有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we were the market disruptor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们是市场颠覆者。

sentences.en: We did cause the fares to be lower.
sentences.zh: 我们确实把机票价格给打下来了。

sentences.en: They called it the Spirit effect.
sentences.zh: 人们称之为“精神效应”。

sentences.en: The first time this really resonated with me was when I was flying back from Fort
sentences.zh: 我第一次真正感受到这一点，是在我从劳德代尔

sentences.en: Lauderdale.
sentences.zh: 堡飞回来的时候。

sentences.en: And I did not have my lanyard on.
sentences.zh: 当时我没挂工牌。

sentences.en: I was out of uniform.
sentences.zh: 我穿的是便服。

sentences.en: And I sat next to this gentleman and his son.
sentences.zh: 我坐在这位先生和他的儿子旁边。

sentences.en: And we had a little bit of turbulence.
sentences.zh: 飞机遇到了一点颠簸。

sentences.en: And then you could hear the hydraulics.
sentences.zh: 接着你能听到液压系统的声音。

sentences.en: And that's always something that either freaks people out or it sounds kind of like a dog.
sentences.zh: 这总会让人感到害怕，或者听起来有点像一只狗的叫声。

sentences.en: It sounds like something...
sentences.zh: 听起来像是某种...

sentences.en: And it's normal.
sentences.zh: 但这很正常。

sentences.en: It's completely normal on the air buses.
sentences.zh: 在空客飞机上这是完全正常的。

sentences.en: And I could see him getting panicked.
sentences.zh: 我能看出他开始惊慌失措了。

sentences.en: So I was like, yes, it's normal.
sentences.zh: 所以我对他说，是的，这很正常。

sentences.en: It's just the hydraulics way.
sentences.zh: 这只是液压系统在运作。

sentences.en: It's okay.
sentences.zh: 没事的。

sentences.en: And so we're sitting there and we're...
sentences.zh: 所以我们就坐在那里……

sentences.en: I'm just kind of talking to him and he like has a moment.
sentences.zh: 我只是在跟他随便聊聊，然后他突然意识到了什么。

sentences.en: And he's like, wait, how did you know that was okay?
sentences.zh: 他说，等等，你怎么知道没事的？

sentences.en: How did you know that sound was?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道那种声音是正常的？

sentences.en: Are you just telling me that?
sentences.zh: 你是不是在瞎编来安抚我？

sentences.en: And I like laughed again.
sentences.zh: 我又笑了笑。

sentences.en: And I was like, I was like, I'm not wearing my lanyard.
sentences.zh: 我说，我没戴工牌呢。

sentences.en: I'm actually a Spirit.
sentences.zh: 其实我是精神航空的员工。

sentences.en: I was like, I promise it's normal.
sentences.zh: 我说，我向你保证这绝对正常。

sentences.en: And he was like, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，哦，这样啊。

sentences.en: Well, then he started talking to me.
sentences.zh: 接着他就开始跟我聊了起来。

sentences.en: And I remember this gentleman being like, you guys make it so affordable for me to take my son on these trips every once in a while.
sentences.zh: 我记得这位先生曾说过：你们让我们偶尔带儿子出去旅行变得如此经济实惠。

sentences.en: You know, it sounded like he shared custody with his son.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，听起来他跟他儿子是共同抚养。

sentences.en: So this was something very special that he liked to do with him when he had him.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他能陪伴孩子时非常喜欢做的一件特别的事。

sentences.en: He was a blue collar worker.
sentences.zh: 他是个蓝领工人。

sentences.en: He was like, I'm terrified of flying.
sentences.zh: 他说，我其实挺恐高的/对坐飞机很恐惧。

sentences.en: But I really love being able to do this and love being able to try taking my son to see different places.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很喜欢能做到这一点，也很高兴能有机会带我儿子去看看不同的地方。

sentences.en: And that was a moment for me that I was just like...
sentences.zh: 那一刻对我来说，我当时的心情是……

sentences.en: Not that I didn't already have pride, but I really started to have pride in Spirit and our brand and what we did and the accessibility that we brought.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说我之前没有自豪感，但我开始真正为精神航空、我们的品牌、我们所做的事以及我们带来的无障碍出行感到自豪。

sentences.en: Because we did.
sentences.zh: 因为我们确实做到了。

sentences.en: We had so many first-time flyers, so many families, so many people that never would have gotten the opportunity to fly if it wasn't for us.
sentences.zh: 我们有那么多第一次坐飞机的乘客、那么多的家庭、那么多如果没有我们，就绝对没有机会坐飞机的人。

sentences.en: And I really loved that we had a carrier that was able to offer that to people.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢我们拥有一家能够为人们提供这种可能性的航空公司。

sentences.en: That you got your seat and you were able to fly the $49 round trip ticket and hop on a flight for the weekend to see your
sentences.zh: 你买个座位就能起飞，花49美元买张往返机票，周末就能跳上飞机去见你的

sentences.en: family that you normally wouldn't have been able to do because all you cared about was getting from point A to point B safely.
sentences.zh: 家人，而这在平时你可能根本负担不起，因为你关心的只是安全地从A点到达B点。

sentences.en: You didn't need the super fancy seats.
sentences.zh: 你不需要超级豪华的座位。

sentences.en: You didn't need the pretzel snacks.
sentences.zh: 你不需要免费的小吃饼干。

sentences.en: You didn't need the single pour of Coca-Cola.
sentences.zh: 你不需要单独倒满的可口可乐。

sentences.en: Like, it was about getting there and it was about the journey that you were going to have once you got there.
sentences.zh: 这一切，全在于抵达目的地，以及当你到达后将经历美妙的旅程。

sentences.en: We were able to connect people that otherwise wouldn't have been able to afford to be connected.
sentences.zh: 我们能够把那些原本因经济原因无法相聚的人们紧紧联系在一起。

sentences.en: So, Naraj, it sounds like at least for a while, Spirit was really making progress, revolutionizing travel.
sentences.zh: 那么，内拉吉（Naraj），听起来至少有一段时间，精神航空确实取得了长足的进步，彻底革新了旅行方式。

sentences.en: When did things start going south?
sentences.zh: 是从什么时候开始情况急转直下的呢？

sentences.en: Well, a few things start to happen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几件事情开始发生了。

sentences.en: The first big thing is that Spirit becomes a victim of its own success.
sentences.zh: 首先发生的重大事情是，精神航空成了自身成功的受害者。

sentences.en: They can't be ignored anymore and they're flying in a lot of places where the big airlines are flying too.
sentences.zh: 他们再也无法被忽视了，并且他们开始飞往许多大型航空公司也在运营的航线。

sentences.en: And so the big airlines introduced something called basic economy, which is basically a Spirit competing fare.
sentences.zh: 于是，各大航司推出了所谓的“基础经济舱”（basic economy），这基本上就是一款用来对标精神航空的票价产品。

sentences.en: It comes with a lot of restrictions.
sentences.zh: 它伴随着许多限制条件。

sentences.en: It doesn't include a checked bag or carry-on bag.
sentences.zh: 其中不包含托运行李或随身行李。

sentences.en: You often can't pick your own seat, but you can pay for those, right?
sentences.zh: 你通常不能自己选座位，但你可以花钱购买这些服务，对吧？

sentences.en: Just like
sentences.zh: 就像

sentences.en: Spirit.
sentences.zh: 精神航空一样。

sentences.en: But the problem is that these bigger airlines, they also have a lot of resources.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这些大型航空公司还拥有大量资源。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because if you have a choice between United and Spirit and they cost the same, you're probably going to go with the bigger airline.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你在联合航空（United）和精神航空之间做选择，而它们的票价一样，你很可能会选择大航空公司。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Spirit may be flying on a route twice a day and United might fly the same route eight times.
sentences.zh: 精神航空一天可能在某条航线上飞两班，而联合航空可能会飞八班。

sentences.en: If your bike gets canceled, there's a backup.
sentences.zh: 如果你的航班被取消了，还有备选方案。

sentences.en: There's also customer service.
sentences.zh: 此外还有客户服务。

sentences.en: There's all these other benefits for flying with the big airlines.
sentences.zh: 搭乘大航空公司的航班还有所有这些其他好处。

sentences.en: And so if you're looking at the same cost, you might be inclined to choose them.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果票价相同，你自然更倾向于选择它们。

sentences.en: And that poses a really big problem for Spirit.
sentences.zh: 这给精神航空带来了非常大的难题。

sentences.en: They can't really lower fares much more than they already have.
sentences.zh: 他们已经很难再把票价压得比现在更低了。

sentences.en: And so to compete with the big airlines, they have to start to improve quality.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了与大航空公司竞争，他们必须开始提升服务质量。

sentences.en: They have to get you to where you're going on time more often.
sentences.zh: 他们必须更频繁地准时把你送达目的地。

sentences.en: They have to have better customer service.
sentences.zh: 他们必须提供更好的客户服务。

sentences.en: And that's expensive.
sentences.zh: 而这成本很高。

sentences.en: And that puts a lot of pressure on Spirit's business model.
sentences.zh: 这给精神航空的商业模式带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: And keep in mind also, the big guys, they have more profitable seats at the front of the plane.
sentences.zh: 还要记住的是，大公司在飞机前部拥有利润更丰厚的座位。

sentences.en: So they can subsidize the basic economy seats.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以用这些来补贴基础经济舱的座位。

sentences.en: Spirit doesn't have that.
sentences.zh: 精神航空可没有这个条件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Spirit does not have a $2,000 business class seat.
sentences.zh: 精神航空没有2000美元的商务舱座位。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So they're feeling the heat from the bigger airlines.
sentences.zh: 所以他们感受到了来自大航空公司的巨大压力。

sentences.en: Tell us sort of what happens from there.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, you know, the pandemic obviously hurts all airlines equally.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，疫情显然对所有航空公司都造成了同样的打击。

sentences.en: But then there's this faster than expected recovery.
sentences.zh: 但随后迎来了比预期更快的复苏。

sentences.en: People really want to travel.
sentences.zh: 人们非常渴望旅行。

sentences.en: And so there's this fierce competition going on.
sentences.zh: 因此，市场上展开了激烈的竞争。

sentences.en: And that keeps scares low, makes it hard for Spirit to earn a profit.
sentences.zh: 这使得票价保持在较低水平，也让精神航空很难赚到利润。

sentences.en: At the same time, a lot of pilots end up retiring during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，许多飞行员在疫情期间选择退休。

sentences.en: But then, you know, in the years after, airlines really need them back.
sentences.zh: 但在疫情之后的几年里，各大航空公司真的非常需要他们回归。

sentences.en: And so they end up paying a lot more to stay competitive.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了保持竞争力，他们最终支付了高昂得多的薪酬。

sentences.en: That starts with the big airlines.
sentences.zh: 这一切是从大型航空公司开始的。

sentences.en: But then everybody else has to do their best to match because there just aren't that many pilots around.
sentences.zh: 但随后其他所有人也都不得不尽最大努力跟进，因为市场上根本没有那么多飞行员。

sentences.en: So, you know, Spirit starts to see that labor, one of their biggest costs is going up.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，精神航空开始发现，劳动力成本这一他们最大的开支之一正在上升。

sentences.en: And their edge is all about costs.
sentences.zh: 而他们的核心优势全在于成本控制。

sentences.en: And if their costs are starting to look a lot like the same costs that the big airlines have, then they've lost their edge.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的成本开始看起来和大航空公司差不多，那么他们就失去了竞争优势。

sentences.en: So they're in this position where costs are rising.
sentences.zh: 因此他们陷入了这样一种境地：成本在上升。

sentences.en: Competition is fierce.
sentences.zh: 竞争异常激烈。

sentences.en: And there are all these other problems that they're just having to deal with.
sentences.zh: 还有所有这些他们不得不应付的其他问题。

sentences.en: And so then they decide they need to do something to get back on track.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定必须采取行动来重回正轨。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜露（Winnalou）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块中“联群结对”（Connections）这款益智游戏的作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基（Sam Azersky）。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作“拼字蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母方块”（Letterboxd）这两款游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“色彩联觉”（promesthesia）的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games 开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: Okay, so at this point, Neeraj, it sounds like Spirit is really getting squeezed in a whole bunch of different ways.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么到了这个阶段，内拉吉，听起来精神航空确实在各个方面都受到了严重挤压。

sentences.en: What do they do to try to get back on track?
sentences.zh: 他们采取了什么措施来试图重回正轨？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, one thing they try to do is they actually try to merge with one of their rivals,
sentences.zh: 对，其中他们尝试做的一件事其实是试图与他们的竞争对手之一合并，

sentences.en: Frontier Airlines, which is another budget carrier.
sentences.zh: 也就是另一家廉价航空公司——边疆航空。

sentences.en: They announced this in 2022.
sentences.zh: 他们在2022年宣布了这一计划。

sentences.en: And the thinking was that they're struggling, things are hard, but if they could create this
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，他们正陷入困境，举步维艰，但如果他们能打造出这个

sentences.en: big national low-cost carrier, that they might actually be able to kind of make some moves.
sentences.zh: 大型全国性低成本航空公司，他们也许真的能够有所作为。

sentences.en: You know, they might be able to take on the bigger airlines in a better way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们或许能以更好的方式向大航空公司发起挑战。

sentences.en: But then JetBlue Airways decides it actually wants to acquire Spirit and it makes a better offer.
sentences.zh: 但随后捷蓝航空决定，它其实想要收购精灵航空，并提出了更好的报价。

sentences.en: And it ends up squeezing Frontier out and they go forward with a JetBlue Spirit merger.
sentences.zh: 这最终挤走了边疆航空，他们继续推进捷蓝与精灵的合并。

sentences.en: But then the Justice Department says, wait a second, we like Spirit.
sentences.zh: 但接着司法部说，等一下，我们挺喜欢精灵的。

sentences.en: Spirit does good things in the airline industry.
sentences.zh: 精灵航空在航空业做得很不错。

sentences.en: It keeps fares low.
sentences.zh: 它能保持低票价。

sentences.en: And so they sue to stop the merger because they're afraid that if JetBlue takes Spirit in, they're going to change the way Spirit's planes work.
sentences.zh: 因此他们提起诉讼阻止合并，因为他们担心如果捷蓝吞并了精灵，会改变精灵飞机的运作方式。

sentences.en: They're going to change the business model and they're going to end up raising fares.
sentences.zh: 他们会改变商业模式，并最终导致票价上涨。

sentences.en: They're basically arguing that if these two airlines merge, it would be bad for consumers.
sentences.zh: 他们的基本论点是，如果这两家航空公司合并，对消费者来说将是不利的。

sentences.en: It's basically an antitrust argument.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一个反垄断论点。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: One of the things that JetBlue said during the merger process is that we're going to take some seats out of Spirit's planes.
sentences.zh: 捷蓝在合并过程中说过的一点是，我们要拆除精灵飞机上的一些座位。

sentences.en: Spirit packs in the seats really tightly to fit as many people as they can on a plane.
sentences.zh: 精灵把座位塞得非常紧，以便在飞机上塞进尽可能多的人。

sentences.en: JetBlue says we're going to add a little legroom, make it a little more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 捷蓝说我们要增加一点腿部空间，让它更舒适一些。

sentences.en: But the Justice Department says, well, wait a second, that means that your costs are going to go up.
sentences.zh: 但司法部说，嗯，等一下，这意味着你们的成本会上升。

sentences.en: You're going to have to charge more to cover them.
sentences.zh: 你们将不得不收取更高费用来弥补这些成本。

sentences.en: And what was Spirit's counterargument to that?
sentences.zh: 那精灵对此的反驳论点是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, Spirit and JetBlue were saying, look, this is going to be good for consumers because we're going to have more market power.
sentences.zh: 你知道，精灵和捷蓝当时说，听着，这对消费者是有利的，因为我们将拥有更大的市场力量。

sentences.en: You know, JetBlue is a low-cost airline.
sentences.zh: 你知道，捷蓝是一家低成本航空公司。

sentences.en: It's not what
sentences.zh: 它不像

sentences.en: Spirit is, but JetBlue does compete to keep fares low and that together, you know, as a national
sentences.zh: 精灵那样，但捷蓝确实通过竞争来保持低票价，而且通过联合起来，你知道，作为一个在所有这些机场运营的全国性

sentences.en: player operating in all these airports, we would be able to actually serve consumers better.
sentences.zh: 参与者，我们实际上能够更好地为消费者服务。

sentences.en: Basically, they're saying if we can pool our resources together, we're going to be able to compete better with the big guys.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们是在说，如果我们能集中资源，我们将能够与大公司展开更好的竞争。

sentences.en: And ergo, we're going to be able to give customers lower fares.
sentences.zh: 从而，我们将能够为客户提供更低的票价。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, with enough scale, we have the resources to keep fares low in a lot more places.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只要有足够的规模，我们就有资源在更多地方保持低票价。

sentences.en: But then the federal court judge decides that Spirit's presence at an airport can lower fares
sentences.zh: 但随后联邦法院法官裁定，精灵在某个机场的存在可以降低

sentences.en: 5-10 percent.
sentences.zh: 5%到10%的票价。

sentences.en: And we need that in the market.
sentences.zh: 而市场上需要这种存在。

sentences.en: And this merger is anti-competitive.
sentences.zh: 这场合并是反竞争的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So merger doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 所以合并没有发生。

sentences.en: Where does Spirit go from here?
sentences.zh: 精灵接下来将走向何方？

sentences.en: So they file for bankruptcy in 2024.
sentences.zh: 因此他们在2024年申请了破产保护。

sentences.en: They get out of bankruptcy in 2025, but then file for bankruptcy again in 2025.
sentences.zh: 他们在2025年走出了破产程序，但随后在2025年又再次申请破产。

sentences.en: And then coming into this year, the Iran war starts.
sentences.zh: 然后到了今年，伊朗战争爆发了。

sentences.en: And that sends fuel prices skyrocketing.
sentences.zh: 这导致燃料价格飙升。

sentences.en: And Spirit has a plan to get out of bankruptcy, but then it seems like with fuel prices this high, that plan is just not going to work.
sentences.zh: 精灵本来有一个走出破产的计划，但现在看来，在燃料价格如此高昂的情况下，这个计划根本行不通了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That would be a challenge for any airline to suddenly have to shoulder these rising fuel
sentences.zh: 对于任何一家航空公司来说，突然不得不承担这些不断上涨的燃料成本都是一个挑战，

sentences.en: costs, but especially a challenge for an airline that has just gone through two bankruptcies and is really trying to keep its costs low to stay competitive.
sentences.zh: 但对于刚刚经历过两次破产、并且竭力保持低成本以维持竞争力的航空公司来说，这尤为艰难。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: You know, labor costs have already gone up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，劳动力成本已经上升了。

sentences.en: Fuel costs are now going up.
sentences.zh: 燃料成本现在也在上升。

sentences.en: Those are the two biggest costs for any airline.
sentences.zh: 这是任何航空公司最大的两项成本。

sentences.en: And so the Trump administration steps in and they say, you know, what can we do?
sentences.zh: 因此特朗普政府介入了，他们说，你知道，我们能做些什么？

sentences.en: These are a lot of jobs.
sentences.zh: 这里有大量的就业岗位。

sentences.en: This is an important airline to the economy.
sentences.zh: 对经济而言，这是一家具备重要意义的航空公司。

sentences.en: And on top of that, presumably the optics of this do not look great, right?
sentences.zh: 除此之外，想必这带来的舆论观感也不太好，对吧？

sentences.en: Having an airline, specifically an airline that caters to working class people, go under because of a war started under the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 眼睁睁看着一家航空公司，特别是迎合工薪阶层需求的航空公司，因为一场在特朗普政府任内爆发的战争而倒闭。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And they float this idea of a $500 million lifeline.
sentences.zh: 他们提出了提供5亿美元救助资金的想法。

sentences.en: The government would step in and lend the company that money, but the government wants protection.
sentences.zh: 政府将介入并向该公司借出这笔资金，但政府想要保障。

sentences.en: You know, they don't want to lend money with no strings attached.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不想无条件地借出资金。

sentences.en: They want to get preferential treatment over the other lenders that have lent Spirit money.
sentences.zh: 他们希望获得比其他曾向精灵借款的债权人更优厚的待遇。

sentences.en: And Spirit's existing lenders don't love that idea.
sentences.zh: 而精灵现有的债权人并不喜欢这个想法。

sentences.en: So they continue talking, but late last week, it becomes clear that there's not really a path forward.
sentences.zh: 于是他们继续谈判，但在上周晚些时候，情况变得明朗，根本没有什么前行之路。

sentences.en: There's just not a deal to be done.
sentences.zh: 根本达不成协议。

sentences.en: And so Spirit's lenders tell Spirit, you know, we think it's time for you to wind down.
sentences.zh: 因此精灵的债权人告诉精灵，你知道，我们认为你们是时候进行清算停业了。

sentences.en: And, you know, they have to move quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们必须迅速行动。

sentences.en: Airlines are expensive.
sentences.zh: 航空公司的运营成本高昂。

sentences.en: You can't announce that an airline is going to shut down weeks in advance because a lot of people are going to start to peel away.
sentences.zh: 你不能提前几周宣布一家航空公司要倒闭，因为很多人会开始纷纷退走。

sentences.en: And so on Friday, they continue flying.
sentences.zh: 所以在周五，他们继续飞行。

sentences.en: They fly 50,000 people.
sentences.zh: 他们运送了5万名旅客。

sentences.en: The last flight in lands in Dallas just after midnight.
sentences.zh: 最后一架航班在午夜刚过时降落在达拉斯。

sentences.en: And Saturday morning at just after 2 a.m., they announce we're done.
sentences.zh: 周六早晨刚过凌晨2点，他们宣布我们完了。

sentences.en: Spirit Airlines is shut down.
sentences.zh: 精灵航空倒闭了。

sentences.en: When did you find out?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候得知这个消息的？

sentences.en: So, this might make me choke up, but at about 11 p.m., we called into a meeting by our ASA
sentences.zh: 这可能会让我哽咽，但在晚上11点左右，我们的ASA国际主席莎拉·尼尔森召集我们开了一个会。

sentences.en: International president, Sarah Nelson.
sentences.zh: 国际主席，莎拉·尼尔森。

sentences.en: I just remember seeing Sarah's face.
sentences.zh: 我只记得看到莎拉的脸。

sentences.en: Sorry, I knew it was over.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我知道一切都结束了。

sentences.en: And she told us it was over.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我们一切都结束了。

sentences.en: And that we were shutting down.
sentences.zh: 我们正在停业关门。

sentences.en: And, uh, we all cried.
sentences.zh: 然后，呃，我们都哭了。

sentences.en: It's been a really crazy, um, 72-ish hours for all of us, um,
sentences.zh: 对我们所有人来说，这真的是非常疯狂的、大约72小时的经历，呃，

sentences.en: because we're losing our family.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在失去我们的家人。

sentences.en: Are you hearing from colleagues and friends?
sentences.zh: 你有没有听到同事和朋友们的消息？

sentences.en: I'm actually, um, I'm, I'm at one of my friends' house with about eight other flights right now.
sentences.zh: 其实我，嗯，我现在在一个朋友家里，和大约其他八名机组人员在一起。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And it, it's like, we're all grieving.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像，我们都在悲痛。

sentences.en: We're all still here.
sentences.zh: 我们都还在这里。

sentences.en: But I think we're, like, grieving the loss because, like, Spirit's the catalyst that, like, brought us all together.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们，就像是在为这种失去而悲伤，因为，精灵就像是把我们所有人凝聚在一起的催化剂。

sentences.en: And, like, that's gone now.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这一切都没了。

sentences.en: And, um, after you've spent years dedicating this time to this company that you had some pride and you believed in and that you loved, and you love the people that you work with,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，当你花了好几年时间把这段时光奉献给这家你曾为之自豪、深信不疑并且热爱、而且你也热爱与你共事的伙伴们的公司时，

sentences.en: it, it just comes in waves.
sentences.zh: 这种情绪是一波接一波袭来的。

sentences.en: It comes in waves.
sentences.zh: 一波接一波。

sentences.en: And, you know, I kind of always thought, like, if something were to happen, like, I would walk away from aviation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我以前总觉得，如果发生了什么事，我会彻底离开航空业。

sentences.en: And that last week, I was like, there's no way.
sentences.zh: 但在上周，我觉得，绝不可能。

sentences.en: There's no way that I can walk away from aviation.
sentences.zh: 我绝不可能离开航空业。

sentences.en: Um, it gets into your, it gets into your bones, aviation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，航空已经融入你的骨髓了。

sentences.en: And I just, like, there's, there's truly, like, thinking back on it.
sentences.zh: 我真的，回想起来，确实是这样。

sentences.en: And then, like, there isn't anything else that, that I want to do.
sentences.zh: 然后，除了这个，真的没有别的我想做的事了。

sentences.en: But there's just something about it.
sentences.zh: 但它就是有一种独特的魔力。

sentences.en: The, you know, the black and yellow in our blood.
sentences.zh: 你知道，黑与黄色流淌在我们的血液里。

sentences.en: That I, you know, it's going to be hard to ever find that again for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我们来说，以后很难再找到那种感觉了。

sentences.en: It's never going to be the same.
sentences.zh: 一切再也回不到从前了。

sentences.en: So, Naraj, we mentioned earlier in our conversation that there's been this outpouring of grief from people who travel, who took spirit, who are so sad that it has gone away.
sentences.zh: 那么，内拉杰，我们在之前的对话中提到，那些曾经出行、乘坐过精灵航空、对它的消失感到万分痛心的乘客们，纷纷表达了他们的哀悼。

sentences.en: Can you just describe for us, what did that grief look like?
sentences.zh: 你能为我们描述一下吗，这种悲痛表现为什么样？

sentences.en: What did it sound like since spirit announced that it was going under on Saturday?
sentences.zh: 自从精灵航空周六宣布倒闭以来，它听起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, I think the immediate reaction for some people was a surprise.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我认为对一些人来说，最初的反应是震惊。

sentences.en: We heard from people at airports on Saturday who had no idea this was coming and showed up and, you know, very quickly had to figure out how they were going to get home.
sentences.zh: 周六我们在机场听到人们说，他们根本不知道会发生这种事，来到机场后，你知道，很快就不得不去想办法怎么回家。

sentences.en: But I think, you know, as frustrated as people were at times with spirit, I think people really started to understand its place and appreciated it for what it was.
sentences.zh: 但我想，你知道，尽管人们有时会对精灵感到沮丧，但我认为人们真的开始理解它的地位，并对它的本质心存感激。

sentences.en: This is a sad day.
sentences.zh: 这是令人悲伤的一天。

sentences.en: Thousands of people that really depend on this low-cost airline to travel that may not have otherwise gone anywhere.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人真的依赖这家低成本航空公司出行，否则他们可能根本不会去任何地方。

sentences.en: And I think seeing it gone is sad for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我想看到它消失对很多人来说是令人难过的。

sentences.en: Spirit was good for, you know, the working consumer who loves to travel, who knows how to pack light.
sentences.zh: 精灵对那些喜欢旅行、懂得精简行李的工薪阶层消费者来说是很好的。

sentences.en: I've taken spirit a lot of places.
sentences.zh: 我坐过精灵去过很多地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, looking online, you see this outpouring of tributes to spirit.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在网上看看，你会看到铺天盖地对精灵的致敬。

sentences.en: This is kind of heartbreaking because whenever I wanted to get, like, a cheap last-minute flight somewhere, I'd be like, let's check spirit.
sentences.zh: 这有点让人心碎，因为每当我想要买一张去某地的便宜的最后一分钟机票时，我就会想，去看看精灵吧。

sentences.en: And now I won't be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 而现在我再也无法那样做了。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of travelers out there who were able to go on vacation because of airlines like Spirit.
sentences.zh: 有许多旅客正是因为有了精灵这样的航空公司，才得以去度假。

sentences.en: Spirit never did me wrong.
sentences.zh: 精灵从来没有对不起我。

sentences.en: Like, do you understand how much flights cost nowadays?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道现在机票有多贵吗？

sentences.en: Like, on some real stuff, flights are super expensive.
sentences.zh: 说实话，机票真的超级贵。

sentences.en: And so it really did have a place for people.
sentences.zh: 所以它对人们来说确实占有一席之地。

sentences.en: What is your diagnosis ultimately, Neeraj, about what Spirit's downfall was?
sentences.zh: 内拉杰，你最终对精灵的倒闭有什么看法？

sentences.en: Like, how much should we attribute to the rising costs associated with the war in Iran or other headwinds faced by budget airlines or the airline industry as a whole?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们应该在多大程度上将之归咎于伊朗战争带来的不断上涨的成本，或是廉价航空公司乃至整个航空业面临的其他逆风？

sentences.en: It's definitely death by a thousand cuts.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是千刀万剐式的死亡。

sentences.en: I mean, Spirit just had an unforgiving few years.
sentences.zh: 我是说，精灵在过去几年里遭遇了残酷的打击。

sentences.en: And they just could not catch a break.
sentences.zh: 他们就是无法获得一丝喘息之机。

sentences.en: They couldn't get stable footing.
sentences.zh: 他们无法站稳脚跟。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think it also shows that this business model itself is really unforgiving.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为这也表明这种商业模式本身确实非常残酷。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of buffer.
sentences.zh: 没有太多的缓冲空间。

sentences.en: And so if one too many things go wrong, it's hard to recover.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要有太多事情出错，就很难恢复过来。

sentences.en: Hindsight is obviously 2020.
sentences.zh: 事后诸葛亮显然是显而易见的。

sentences.en: But how should we be thinking about the merger that the DOJ blocked in 2024?
sentences.zh: 但我们该如何看待司法部在2024年阻止的那场合并呢？

sentences.en: Because at the time, Spirit said, we need this.
sentences.zh: 因为当时精灵说，我们需要这个。

sentences.en: The DOJ obviously didn't buy that argument.
sentences.zh: 司法部显然不买账。

sentences.en: And now here we are.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们落得这般田地。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really set off this political debate.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实引发了政治争论。

sentences.en: The Trump administration says, you know, look, the Biden administration interfered and now Spirit's going under.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府说，你看，拜登政府进行了干预，现在精灵倒闭了。

sentences.en: And some experts I've talked to agree.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的一些专家也表示赞同。

sentences.en: They say that, you know, had this merger gone forward, this new combined airline might have been able to survive and be vibrant and lower fares across the country.
sentences.zh: 他们说，如果当初合并得以推进，这个新的合并后的航空公司或许能够生存下来，充满活力，并降低全国各地的票价。

sentences.en: But then a lot of experts aren't so sure.
sentences.zh: 但也有许多专家并不那么确定。

sentences.en: Airline mergers are notoriously difficult to pull off.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，航空公司合并极难成功。

sentences.en: They cost lots of money.
sentences.zh: 它们耗资巨大。

sentences.en: And there's just no guarantee that it would have ended well for JetBlue and Spirit.
sentences.zh: 而且根本无法保证这对捷蓝和精灵来说会有好的结局。

sentences.en: I want to talk about what Spirit's demise means for the future of air travel more broadly.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈精灵的消亡对未来航空旅行的更广泛影响。

sentences.en: Like, since they came on the scene, there have been other low-cost budget airlines like Frontier and Allegiant.
sentences.zh: 比如，自从它们崭露头角以来，还出现过其他廉价航空公司，比如边疆航空和忠实航空。

sentences.en: So what does the collapse of Spirit mean for those guys, if anything?
sentences.zh: 那么精灵的倒闭对这些同行意味着什么（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: It's a mixed picture.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的情况。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Allegiant, and they actually adopted this model around the same time as Spirit.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了忠实航空，他们其实和精神航空差不多在同一时期采用了这种模式。

sentences.en: And they have actually done pretty well.
sentences.zh: 而且他们实际上做得相当不错。

sentences.en: They just actually are in the middle of acquiring another airline, Sun Country.
sentences.zh: 他们目前正处于收购另一家航空公司——太阳国航空的过程中。

sentences.en: And part of the reason for their success is, unlike Spirit, Allegiant was able to stay off the radar of the big airlines.
sentences.zh: 他们成功的部分原因在于，与精神航空不同，忠实航空能够避开大型航空公司的雷达。

sentences.en: About 75% of their routes, they have zero competition.
sentences.zh: 在大约75%的航线上，他们没有任何竞争对手。

sentences.en: But, you know, others, not so much.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，其他航空公司就没那么幸运了。

sentences.en: Frontier, like Spirit, is facing a lot of the same probleMs.
sentences.zh: 边疆航空和精神航空一样，正面临着许多相同的问题。

sentences.en: I do wonder also about the bigger airlines, the Uniteds, the Americans, etc.
sentences.zh: 我也很好奇那些大型航空公司，比如联合航空、美国航空等情况如何。

sentences.en: Like, I do wonder whether the bigger guys will now have just that much less incentive to offer competitive low-cost fares.
sentences.zh: 比如说，我很想知道这些大公司现在提供具有竞争力的低价机票的动力是否会大大减少。

sentences.en: Do you foresee that happening?
sentences.zh: 你预见到这种情况会发生吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The experts that I talk to do think that fares are going to rise.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的专家确实认为票价将会上涨。

sentences.en: And they say that, to some extent, that probably was going to happen anyway.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，在某种程度上，这可能本来就会发生。

sentences.en: Fuel costs have gone up.
sentences.zh: 燃油成本已经上升了。

sentences.en: Airlines have to cover that.
sentences.zh: 航空公司必须承担这些费用。

sentences.en: But for the big airlines, they're so much more focused on the elite traveler.
sentences.zh: 但对于大型航空公司来说，他们更加专注于高端旅客。

sentences.en: They have really discovered that in the last few years, that if they invest in those people who are willing to spend a lot of money, they can earn a lot of profit.
sentences.zh: 他们在过去几年里确实发现，如果他们投资于那些愿意花大钱的人，他们就能获得巨额利润。

sentences.en: And it's worked exceptionally well for airlines like Delta and United.
sentences.zh: 这对于达美航空和联合航空这样的公司来说效果异常显著。

sentences.en: They've invested in lounges.
sentences.zh: 他们投资了贵宾休息室。

sentences.en: They've invested in their loyalty prograMs.
sentences.zh: 他们投资了常旅客计划。

sentences.en: They've invested in fancy seats and plane renovations.
sentences.zh: 他们投资了豪华座椅和飞机改造。

sentences.en: And it's really paying off.
sentences.zh: 这确实带来了丰厚的回报。

sentences.en: And so will they still compete for basic economy travelers?
sentences.zh: 那么他们还会争夺基础经济舱旅客吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Those are travelers that they see maybe someday upgrading to main economy and up to business class.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这些旅客也许有一天会升级到普通经济舱甚至商务舱。

sentences.en: But right now, those airlines are really focused on the front of the plane, those nice, big, fancy seats.
sentences.zh: 但现在，这些航空公司真正关注的是飞机前部那些舒适、宽敞、豪华的座位。

sentences.en: It's interesting because the spirit era was really marked by these airlines stripping amenities out from what they offered so that they could offer low-budget fares.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为精神航空时代的标志正是这些航空公司剥离了提供的各种便利设施，以便能够提供低预算机票。

sentences.en: But what you are describing sounds like almost going in the opposite direction, like more and more offering these luxury amenities.
sentences.zh: 但你所描述的听起来几乎是在朝相反的方向发展，也就是越来越多地提供这些豪华便利设施。

sentences.en: And it feels as though what you are describing is a real widening of the division that already exists in air travel and so many other facets of American life between the haves and the have-nots.
sentences.zh: 感觉你所描述的是航空旅行以及美国生活的许多其他方面中，早已存在的富裕阶层与贫困阶层之间分化的真正扩大。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, I mean, Spirit in its early years really democratized air travel.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，我的意思是，精神航空在早期确实让航空旅行平民化了。

sentences.en: But even before it shut down, Spirit was embracing catering to the premium travelers.
sentences.zh: 但甚至在倒闭之前，精神航空就已经开始迎合高端旅客了。

sentences.en: They last summer announced plans to add premium seats at the front of their planes.
sentences.zh: 他们去年夏天宣布了在飞机前部增加高端座位的计划。

sentences.en: And they actually started to rebundle their fares so that you could buy a single ticket that included a lot of the things that they once stripped out.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上开始重新打包票价，这样你就可以买一张包含许多他们曾经剥离掉的服务的单程票。

sentences.en: So even before Spirit went under, we were already starting to see a retreat from that business model that was just sharply focused on low costs and low fares.
sentences.zh: 因此，甚至在精神航空倒闭之前，我们就已经开始看到他们从那种单纯专注于低成本和低票价的商业模式中退缩了。

sentences.en: And so there's this sense that, yeah, maybe the industry is headed in a direction where it's not as focused on serving everybody.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种感觉，是的，也许这个行业正在朝着一个不再那么专注于服务所有人的方向发展。

sentences.en: Neeraj, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 最后，20世纪创建了CNN的传媒巨头特德·特纳于周三去世，享年87岁。
